title: Classical music, rock and jazz
summary: She learned classics from the player piano and won't play rock because it stiffens her feel.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: You have always worked with black music, right or not?
Well, what do you mean when you say that?
This is what you've been playing.
That's what I like but I haven't always done that. I learned the classics through the set player. I had to get my other 50¢ a week.
Would you have liked to have played classical music?

No, I don't think so. A concert pianist told me - Robert Harris been trying to get me to do that. He heard me when I was really in good form at the Hickory House. You know, the same reason I won't play commercial rock. Commercial rock makes you corny. Jazz pushes off, you know, like an eighth note tied/over to a quarter in the next bar. It pushes off, it goes easy, like this, but rock, 1-2-3-4-bop, like that... I don't want to get stiff like that. I had a drummer and a bass player to kind of stiffen me out a couple of times.
